messages.subject: Cam trap video footage - Data extraction - Excel or R?
messages.subject_clean: Cam trap video footage - Data extraction - Excel or R?
messages.body_plain:
Hi

Sorry for the long message...

I have 24 hours 12 months of video footage (5 min videos, 1 min before activation of camera).
Videos are extracted to obtain 5 images (you can imagine how many images I have!), which are then run through while visually checking for anything from insects to large animals using termite mounds or hollows in termite mounds and eating termites
Rain also recorded.
I have an Excel spreadsheet where I paste metadata into the rest I have drop-downs where applicable.
If no interaction with the termite mound or hollow usage metadata is available but the rest of the line no data entry (spreadsheet).

It is a lot of work and extremely tiring on one's eyes.
Is it better to do it this way than import data from the spreadsheets into R?
I am new to R and currently busy working through R FOR DUMMIES.

This is for my MSc degree. I have a year to learn R, go through all the video footage, and get the raw data. I'm not even thinking of the stats in R at the moment.
Is there an easier way to do all this? Should I rather directly use camtrapR and where do I start??

Thanks
F

Hi,
db_directory refers to the directory containing the digikam4.db file.

By default digiKam saves it in:
C:\Users\USERNAME\Pictures

I don't know the default for Linux or MacOS, but you can find the path in the digiKam settings > Configure Digikam > Database

Hello,
it sounds like camtrapR might help, especially if you are using it for images and can tag them (species ID, event type, weather, or whatever). Do you tag images (e.g. digiKam), and do you create the tables with the metadata automatically? If not (and you are doing it manually), then I am positive camtrapR can help. How exactly would depend on your data.

Since you are new to R I'd suggest to first learn the basics and then see if your workflow may be compatible with camtrapR. The package has some sample data included, but basic R skills are required.
Feel free to share more specific questions if you have.
Best regards,

messages.subject: Re: Installation of camtrapR failed
messages.body_plain:
I solved the install problems by installing the dependencies directly from the c2d4u Ubuntu repository of CRAN as follows:

sudo apt update
sudo apt install r-cran-units
sudo apt install r-cran-terra
sudo apt install r-cran-s2
and so on...

The R package "camtrapR" was not found in the c2d4u repository; therefore, I installed "camtrapR" from within R (using  install.packages()) after the dependencies had been installed.

messages.subject: Detection history for multispecies occupancy models
messages.subject_clean: Detection history for multispecies occupancy models
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone!

I am working on the camera trap-based species richness and its relation to anthropogenic and environmental covariates in a ~11,000 sqkm human-dominated forested landscape, with the help of multi-species occupancy models. However, due to logistic constraints, camera traps were not deployed simultaneously or at one go to cover the entire study area. Instead, there were multiple blocks in different time periods, and it took ~1.5 years to complete the survey. Since I have different record tables for different blocks, I wondered how to create a single list of detection history from these multiple record tables to run the multispecies occupancy models. Or is there any other way to address this issue?
In this context, any suggestion/guidance is highly appreciated.

Thank you in advance!

Cheers
Sankarshan
